content_en.prompt: Rani, Meera, Ehan, Omkar, Yash, Bahar and Ninad have applied for open positions in a factory's accounting, warehouse, call center, and packing departments. Each person is only qualified for the jobs shown in a figure; one person must be hired per position, and each person can hold at most one job.
content_en.question: Which of the following is definitely true?

options.text: Nahid will be hired for packing.
Yash will be hired for the warehouse.
Omkar will be hired for packing.
If Meera is hired for packing, Bahar will be hired for accounting.

content_en.explanation: If a job has only one applicant, that applicant must be hired there even if qualified for other jobs too — Omkar is the only applicant for the call center, so he must be hired there (making option C false). Removing Omkar and the call center from consideration, the same logic now applies to the warehouse: Yash is the only remaining qualified applicant, so Yash must be hired for the warehouse — option B is true. Removing Yash and the warehouse, the remaining assignments are no longer forced: e.g. Meera and Rani could be hired for packing and accounting respectively, which violates options A and D — so those options are not definitely true.
content_en.ct_explanation: We used a bipartite graph to represent the data structure of jobs and applicants — an interesting way of representing a graph using two categories of vertices, which allows a polynomial-time algorithm to solve the underlying vertex-matching problem. This is a constraint satisfaction problem, common in many real-world resource allocation problems and puzzles (like Sudoku): assigning a value to one variable eliminates options for others. We used decomposition by considering each job on its own, independent of the others, and logic by repeatedly applying the rule 'if a job has only one applicant, that applicant must be hired there' — finding an algorithm to solve the task step by step, which is itself an exercise in computational thinking.

content_zh.prompt: Rani、Meera、Ehan、Omkar、Yash、Bahar和Ninad應徵了一間工廠的職缺，包括會計、倉儲、客服中心和包裝部門。每個人只符合圖中所示的特定職缺資格；每個職位都必須有一個人被錄取，而且每個人最多只能擔任一個職位。
content_zh.question: 下面哪一項敘述一定是真的？

options.text: 如果Meera被錄取到包裝部門，Bahar就會被錄取到會計部門。

content_zh.explanation: 如果某個職位只有一位應徵者符合資格，那麼即使這個人也符合其他職缺的資格，這個職位也一定會錄取他——Omkar是唯一符合客服中心資格的應徵者，所以他一定會被錄取到客服中心（因此選項C是錯的）。把Omkar和客服中心從考量中移除後，同樣的邏輯這時適用在倉儲部門：Yash是剩下唯一符合倉儲資格的應徵者，所以Yash一定會被錄取到倉儲部門——選項B成立。再把Yash和倉儲部門移除後，剩下的職缺分配就不再是唯一確定的了：例如Meera和Rani有可能分別被錄取到包裝和會計部門，這樣就違反了選項A和D——所以這兩個選項不一定成立。
content_zh.ct_skills: 分解、演算法思維（Decomposition, Algorithmic Thinking）
content_zh.ct_explanation: 我們用一張「二分圖」來表示職缺和應徵者之間的資料結構——這是一種有趣的圖表示法，用兩類不同的頂點來表示資料，讓「頂點配對問題」能用多項式時間的演算法解決。這是一個「限制滿足問題」，在許多現實世界的資源分配問題和益智遊戲（例如數獨）裡都很常見：替一個變數指定一個值，就會排除掉其他變數的某些選項。我們運用了分解——把每個職缺獨立分開來考慮，不受其他職缺影響；也運用了邏輯——反覆套用「如果某職缺只有一位符合資格的應徵者，這個人就一定會被錄取」這條規則，一步步找出解題的演算法，這本身就是一次運算思維的練習。
